D005-D006_h001.question:
I’ve been feeling really off for about two months now. Things at work are piling up—weddings, deadlines, client demands—but my head’s been somewhere else. I keep hearing my client’s fiancé, Mark, talking to me at night. Not just once—he says things like, “I know how you feel,” and “We’re meant to be.” I don’t see him, but his voice is so clear, like he’s standing right there. I know it sounds strange, but I really believe he’s trying to reach out, that he’s in love with me. He doesn’t say it out loud, of course, but I can *feel* it. He smiles at me in a certain way. He lingers after meetings.

There were a few weeks where I couldn’t sleep for days. I was making plans—so many plans—fixing three weddings at once, booking venues in other states, charging it all. I felt unstoppable. But then the voices got louder. Now, even when I’m not revved up, when I’m quiet with my husband, they’re still there. He says he doesn’t hear them, but I do. I don’t know how long this’s been going on exactly—some days it’s worse than others. I just know Mark’s involved, and I need to be ready when he comes.
D005-D006_h001.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D005-D006_h001.answer: C & D. Schizophrenia & Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D005-D006_h002.question:
Lately, things have felt… off. For about two months now, I’ve been seeing people out of the corner of my eye—figures in the store aisles, even when I know I’m alone. Last week, I swear I saw a man in a black coat standing by the fridge during my shift. But when I turned the camera back, no one was there. It’s like my eyes are playing tricks, but it feels too real to ignore. I’ve started thinking the cameras aren’t just for security—like they’re watching *me*, not the customers. Not just the store cameras, either. I feel like my phone’s tracking me, maybe the government, or someone sending signals through the streetlights. I can’t shake the feeling they’re testing something on me.

I’ve had a few nights where sleep felt pointless—like I had too much energy, too many thoughts racing. I cleaned the whole store twice in one night, restocked everything in record time. I felt sharp, unstoppable, like I could handle anything. But those bursts don’t last. And sometimes, the visions stick around even when I’m not high-energy—just there, quiet, like background noise. I can’t tell what’s real anymore.
D005-D006_h002.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D005-D006_h002.answer: C & D. Schizophrenia & Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D005-D006_h003.question:
I’ve been feeling like something’s off for about two months now. At first, it was just a sense that people were watching me—cops, coworkers, even strangers on the train. I started noticing cameras everywhere, and I swear I’d feel someone brushing up behind me, but when I turned, no one was there. The touching part… it’s like bugs crawling under my skin or fingers tracing my arms. No rash, no bugs—just the feeling. I checked the lights, too. On tour last month, I kept thinking the lighting cues were sending me coded messages. Not random—like they were meant for me.

Around the same time, I was sleeping less, maybe two hours a night, but I had this unstoppable energy. I’d rewrite entire rigging plans in my head, convinced I’d invent something revolutionary. Talked nonstop at work—guys told me I was “wired.” But that only lasted a few days here and there. Mostly, I’ve just felt paranoid, on edge, like everyone’s in on something. There were moments I felt high-strung, almost electric, but they’d fade. The worst part is not knowing what's real.
D005-D006_h003.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D005-D006_h003.answer: C & D. Schizophrenia & Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D005-D006_h004.question:
I’ve been hearing things—voices—talking to me about how special I am, how *he* chose me. At first, it was just whispers during practice, but now they’re clear, like someone’s standing behind me. They tell me my idol, the leader of the senior group—he’s been sending me secret signals during concerts, that he loves me and wants us to be together. I know it sounds crazy, but I can *feel* it’s real. Sometimes, when I’m alone in the dorm, I hear him calling my name.  

The past two months have been… intense. I don’t sleep much—like, only two or three hours, but I don’t feel tired. I’ve been choreographing non-stop, writing songs at 3 a.m., sending them to managers even if they don’t ask. I feel electric, like I’m finally unlocking my purpose. But then, out of nowhere, I’ll freeze up during rehearsal, convinced the other trainees are mimicking the voices, testing me.  

It’s hard to focus. Some days I’m on top of the world, and others, I just sit in the practice room crying, hearing the voices say I’ve betrayed him. I don’t know what’s real anymore. The mania—I don’t even know how long it’s lasted. It’s like time’s been stretched. And the voices? They never really stop.
D005-D006_h004.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D005-D006_h004.answer: C & D. Schizophrenia & Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D005-D006_h005.question:
I’ve been struggling for about two months now—maybe a little longer. Things feel… different. Unsettled. Lately, I keep sensing someone touching me when no one’s there—like a hand on my shoulder or fingers brushing my arm. It’s subtle, but it’s there. And there’s this woman from the congregation—she doesn’t know I exist, really, but I’m certain she’s been sending me silent messages of love. She smiles during sermons, and I know it’s meant for me. God speaks through her in ways others wouldn’t understand.

There’ve been times when I’m up for hours past midnight—writing sermons, praying, pacing. My mind races, and I feel this fire, like I’m on a divine mission. But then it fades—some days I feel normal, maybe a little tired. The visions or feelings of her love—they haven’t stopped, though they come and go. When I’m not feeling “elevated,” those sensations on my skin still linger. I don’t know if it’s spiritual warfare, a test, or something else. 

My wife’s worried. I don’t want to alarm anyone, but I can’t ignore what I’m feeling—what I *know*. Still, I go to work. I preach. I function. I just don’t feel grounded the way I used to.
D005-D006_h005.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D005-D006_h005.answer: C & D. Schizophrenia & Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D005-D006_h006.question:
I’ve been… off… for about seven months now. It started at work—old COBOL systems, you know, quiet, predictable. But then I started noticing things. My boss coughed during a meeting—three times—and I knew it was coded, meant for me. Traffic signs flashing “DON’T WALK” at empty intersections? That was a signal, too. They’re watching, feeding info through the radio static in my car.  

Sometimes I’ll stand in the hallway at home, mid-step, arms raised like I’m reaching for a shelf, and just… stay. My neighbor saw me once through the window. I didn’t move for ten minutes. I couldn’t explain why. It just felt necessary.  

I haven’t touched my hobbies. The model trains I used to build with my son? Dusty. Can’t seem to start anything anymore.  

But—there were a few weeks… I don’t sleep much, ever, but then I didn’t sleep at all and didn’t need to. I rewrote 20 years of legacy payroll scripts in four days, thought I’d cracked some financial prophecy in the hex codes. Felt bulletproof. That passed. Now I’m just tired again.  

Do those highs count? Were they real? I can’t tell if they were part of the illness or just… me, surging. The voices don’t stop, not really. But the energy? It flickers.
D005-D006_h006.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Schizophrenia
D005-D006_h006.answer: D & C. Schizophrenia & Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D005-D006_h007.question:
I’ve been off since last winter—about seven months now, I guess. At first, I thought it was just stress. I work from home tutoring kids in math and English, so when I stopped showering or changing clothes for days, my ex pointed it out during visitation. I didn’t care. Getting dressed felt pointless. Even turning on the lights was too much.  

Then the pain started—deep inside my ribs, like my liver was rotting. Doctors ran tests, said everything’s fine, but I *know* it’s not. Something’s wrong with my organs. I can *feel* it decaying.  

Sometimes I catch myself copying my son’s fidgeting—tapping my fingers just like he does, even when I’m alone. I don’t mean to. It just happens.  

There were a few weeks in spring where I barely slept, but I was cleaning for hours, rearranging furniture at 3 a.m., texting old coworkers nonstop. I felt unstoppable—like my brain was on fast-forward. But that faded. Now I’m just… stuck. Can’t focus. Can’t start lessons on time. My students’ parents are pulling their kids.  

I don’t know if it’s depression, nerves, or something worse. The energy comes and goes, but the thoughts—the beliefs about my body, the way I mimic people—they haven’t left.
D005-D006_h007.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Schizophrenia
D005-D006_h007.answer: D & C. Schizophrenia & Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D005-D006_h008.question:
I’ve been off since about seven months ago—right after I got recognized in that music journal for my teaching. At first, it felt like everything was clicking: I started believing I could compose a symphony that would change contemporary piano music forever—like I was chosen for it, meant to reveal some hidden musical code only I could hear. I’d stay up for hours, hands moving over silent keys, mapping out movements no one else would understand. I catch myself doing it even now, my fingers tapping the same sequence over and over, even when I’m not at a piano.

I don’t feel flat, exactly—but my husband says I don’t react like I used to. No surprise, no tears, even when he tries to talk about how worried he is. My voice just stays even. My eyes stay ahead.

There were times—maybe a few weeks last winter—when I felt electric, like I didn’t need sleep, like my thoughts were faster and brighter. I signed up for three performance competitions I didn’t enter, filled notebooks with plans. But those bursts didn’t last. Now, even without that rush, the thoughts stay: the messages in the music, the purpose in my hands. I can’t tell what’s real anymore—but it all feels true.
D005-D006_h008.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Schizophrenia
D005-D006_h008.answer: D & C. Schizophrenia & Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D005-D006_h009.question:
I’ve been off for about seven months now—ever since I didn’t get that role in the indie film I was up for. It feels like my body’s betraying me. I’m convinced something’s wrong inside—like my organs are shrinking or poisoning me. Doctors say there’s nothing, but I *feel* it. It’s real to me.  

I’ve stopped going to auditions. My agent calls, but I won’t answer. It’s not that I don’t want to—I just… can’t. Instructions, questions, even simple things like “Get up” or “Eat something”—they hit me like noise. No point. No movement.  

My mom says I sound flat, like a robot. I don’t mean to. It’s just… nothing feels like it matters. Faces blur. Voices fade. I don’t cry. I don’t laugh. Even when I wanted to act, I couldn’t summon anything real.  

There were times—maybe a few weeks total—where I felt electric. Too alive. Talked fast, barely slept, thought I could write and star in my own movie overnight. But that energy always crashed. Now I don’t know if it was real or just my head playing tricks. It’s not like that anymore. Most of the time, I’m just… empty.  

I can’t tell what’s illness, what’s the grind of not working, or if any of it ever mattered.
D005-D006_h009.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Schizophrenia
D005-D006_h009.answer: D & C. Schizophrenia & Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D005-D006_h010.question:
I’ve been having a lot of strange thoughts lately—like my blood is poison or my heart’s not real. I can *feel* it pumping wrong, even though doctors say I’m fine. It’s been going on for months… maybe around seven? I don’t smile much anymore, even when I want to. My face just... won’t move right. Sometimes I make weird faces without meaning to—like twisting my mouth—and people stare.  

I used to throw myself into painting, but now my body feels like it doesn’t belong to me. My emotions are flat, like I’m watching life through a cracked window. But… there were times—few of them—when I barely slept, and my ideas raced so fast I couldn’t keep up. I’d paint for hours, convinced my art could change the world. That felt powerful, not sick. Still, those bursts didn’t last long. I can’t say exactly how long they went—maybe a few days? Not weeks or anything.  

There were moments, though, when I heard whispers in empty rooms—just vague murmurs, like someone turning the radio on and off. I don’t know if it’s stress, creativity, or something else. I just know I’m not the same person I was before.
D005-D006_h010.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Schizophrenia
D005-D006_h010.answer: D & C. Schizophrenia & Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D005-D006_h011.question:
I’ve been feeling... different… for about four months now. It started with this strange confidence—like I wasn’t just a cab driver anymore. I remember thinking I could predict people’s lives just by looking at them, like I had some kind of gift. Passengers would mention their problems, and I’d tell them things—fate, destiny—and it all made perfect sense to me. Sometimes, I’d repeat what they said, not on purpose, just… it came out. My ex-wife said it was creepy.  

The past few months haven’t been stable. There were times I barely slept, didn’t need to. Felt sharp, like my brain was faster than everyone else’s. I drove all night, didn’t feel tired. Talked a lot. Maybe too much. But it’s not like that all the time. There were days I stayed in bed, hearing the same phrases loop in my head—things I’d said or someone once told me, echoing.  

I don’t know if it’s mood or the thoughts or both. The energy came and went, but the sense that I’m meant for something bigger hasn’t fully left. And the repeating… that still happens. I can’t tell what’s real half the time, but I’m not sure if it’s one thing or two tangled together.
D005-D006_h011.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    D. Delusional Disorder
D005-D006_h011.answer: A & B. Schizophrenia & Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D005-D006_h012.question:
I’ve been feeling… off… for about four months now. It started with this sense that people were watching me—cameras in my apartment, neighbors talking about me, even the way strangers look at me on the bus feels intentional, like they’re part of something. I know it sounds crazy, but I can *feel* it. Sometimes, I’ll stand in one spot for a long time, just holding a position—like, I’ll raise my arms and keep them there, not because it feels good, but because my body doesn’t feel like mine anymore. It’s like I’m resisting something invisible.

There’ve been times when my thoughts race so fast I can’t sleep, not because I’m tired, but because my brain won’t shut off. I’ll talk fast, feel super confident, like I could write a book in one night or solve world problems. But those times never last long—maybe a few days, then they fade. The paranoia and the weird body sensations stick around longer. I don’t know what’s real anymore. I used to apply for jobs, but now I just can’t bring myself to leave the house. I don’t know if I’m sick, or if the world actually has it in for me—or both.
D005-D006_h012.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    D. Delusional Disorder
D005-D006_h012.answer: A & B. Schizophrenia & Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D005-D006_h013.question:
I’ve been feeling really off for about four months now. At first, it was just this nagging thought—like, deep down I knew my boyfriend was cheating, even though he denies it and there’s no proof. I see the way people look at him when we’re out, the barista at the other café winks—like they’re in on it. I started changing how I dress, avoiding eye contact, but I can’t stop watching, you know?  

Sometimes, I catch myself doing these little things—tapping the sugar packets in a pattern, arranging liddles just so—like if I don’t, something bad will happen. It feels silly, but it’s like my hands have their own mind.  

There were weeks where I barely slept, but I was fine—actually great, buzzing. I cleaned the apartment three times in one weekend, texted strangers about my “vision” for a coffee blend. I felt powerful. But that passed. Now I’m just tired.  

The thing is, I don’t know if I ever fully believed the cheating part… or if that even matters. The thoughts come and go. And the energy—some days I’m lit up, others I can’t stand the noise in the café. I just… don’t feel like me.
D005-D006_h013.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    D. Delusional Disorder
D005-D006_h013.answer: A & B. Schizophrenia & Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D005-D006_h014.question:
I’ve been off since about four months ago, right after that big deal in the city fell through—first time I’d lost a contract like that in years. At first, I thought it was stress, but then things started feeling… wrong. I became certain something terrible was coming—like the world was ending, not in a fiery way, but just… dissolving. People don’t get it, but I *know* it’s real. Like everything—homes, families, even time—is just going to vanish.  

I still show houses, but some days, my arms just… stay up, like if someone lifts them, they stay there. My assistant joked I was “posing for a mannequin ad,” but I couldn’t move for a while. It wasn’t on purpose.  

And there were times I didn’t sleep—three nights straight—and I’d call ten clients at once, redesigning listings in my head, convinced I was reinventing real estate. That energy? It burned out fast, though. Now it’s mostly this dread, even when I feel clear.  

I can’t say exactly how long the highs lasted… a week? Less? They came and went. The fear and the not-moving—those stick around more. But if I’m honest, I don’t know what’s illness and what’s just me unraveling.
D005-D006_h014.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    D. Delusional Disorder
D005-D006_h014.answer: A & B. Schizophrenia & Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D005-D006_h015.question:
I’ve been feeling… off… for about four months now. It started small—like, I’d hear my coworkers say something and then I’d catch myself repeating it, almost like an echo. I didn’t even realize I was doing it until one of them laughed and asked if I was mimicking her. That embarrassed me, so I tried to stop, but it keeps happening, especially when I’m stressed.

But the thoughts… they’re getting worse. I keep thinking the world’s about to end—like not in a “climate change” way, but that everything is fake and going to just… collapse. Like, pets, my apartment, even me—I feel like we’re all just temporary. Sometimes I tell my clients their dogs don’t matter anymore because “nothing will in a few weeks.” I know that sounds crazy, but it feels so real.

There were a few weeks where I barely slept, but didn’t feel tired—like I could groom eight dogs in a row and still clean the shop after. I talked fast, joked too much, felt like I was on a high. But that’s faded. Now I’m just drained… except the bad thoughts won’t leave. I can’t tell if the energy before was real or part of this whole mess. I don’t know how long it lasted, honestly—maybe a week? Less?
D005-D006_h015.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    D. Delusional Disorder
D005-D006_h015.answer: A & B. Schizophrenia & Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D005-D006_h016.question:
I’ve been struggling for about three months now—maybe longer, it’s hard to track. At work, the auction house feels different. People’s laughter, side comments… I can’t shake the feeling they’re coded, meant for me. Once, a bidder whispered to his friend, and I *knew* they were talking about my tie—it wasn’t just a tie, it was a signal.  

I hear things too—voices when no one’s around. Not full conversations, just fragments. Like someone muttering my name during silence, or a radio playing just behind the wall. I turn, and nothing’s there.  

Speaking’s gotten messy. My thoughts feel like they’re colliding. I’ll start explaining something to my wife, and the words… tangle. She says I’m not making sense. I know what I mean, but getting it out right? It slips.  

I’ve stopped going out. Even with friends I’ve known for years. It’s not that I don’t care—I do, I love my wife—but being around people? It’s exhausting.  

There were a few weeks where I barely slept, but I felt wired, like I could run auctions for days straight without rest. That passed. Now I just feel drained. I don’t know how much of this is stress, or something else. The energy surge? It came and went, but I can’t say if it was part of this… or a separate thing.
D005-D006_h016.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D005-D006_h016.answer: B & D. Schizophrenia & Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D005-D006_h017.question:
I’ve been struggling for about three months now—ever since I started noticing this strange smell, like something’s rotting behind the walls. No one else smells it, not even my husband. I told the museum staff and had the ventilation checked, but they said everything’s fine. Still, I can’t shake it. Sometimes it feels like it’s coming from inside me, like my insides are decaying. The doctors can’t find anything, but I *know* something’s wrong with my body.

Lately, my thoughts get tangled. I’ll try to explain what I’m feeling, and the words just... fall apart. Even I don’t understand what I’m saying sometimes. I’ve stopped talking much because of it. People say I look flat, like I don’t care, but it’s not that—I just can’t seem to show it.

There was a week in January when I barely slept, full of energy, convinced I could redesign all the exhibit labels in one night. But that passed quickly. Now, I just feel numb, and that smell... it never leaves.
D005-D006_h017.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D005-D006_h017.answer: B & D. Schizophrenia & Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D005-D006_h018.question:
I’ve been feeling off for about three months now. Things don’t taste right—like, yesterday I bit into a sandwich and it suddenly tasted like metal, even though nothing was on it. It happens more than once. People think I’m crazy, but I *know* the foreman’s daughter, she keeps giving me these soft looks, smiling at me when no one’s watching. She don’t say much, but I *know* she feels something. I call her “Lumina”—she *shines*. Words just come to me now—“Veridown,” “Zeltops”—they make sense in my head, help me keep things straight.

I used to love hanging out after work, joking around, maybe grabbing a drink. Now? Nothing feels fun. Music, food, even sunsets—everything’s flat. But some days, man, I feel like I could build a whole house by myself in one shift. I don’t need sleep, don’t need breaks. My brain’s racing, ideas flying, but then… it just crashes.

There are times I’m fine, just the voices and tastes and Lumina… but the energy? It comes and goes. I can’t tell if it’s part of the same thing or something else entirely. Some days I’m fired up, others I’m just numb, watching the world move by.
D005-D006_h018.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D005-D006_h018.answer: B & D. Schizophrenia & Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D005-D006_h019.question:
I’ve been feeling off for about three months now. At work, the kitchen gets so loud, but not from the pots or machines—it’s like people talking, watching me. I see figures in the corner when I’m scrubbing pans, shadows standing by the fire exit, but when I turn, no one’s there. I know it sounds strange, but I can’t shake the feeling they’re filming me—cameras in the vents, maybe the health inspector’s involved. I call it the “chrome net”—it hums when the ovens are on. That’s what I told my coworker, but he just stared.

I used to love dancing to old records on weekends, but now, nothing lifts me. Even tea with my sister feels like chore. I stopped going to church—what’s the point if they’re all in on it?

Some days, my head races, like I could clean the whole kitchen in ten minutes, and I don’t need sleep. I talk fast, maybe too much, but it’s not like that all the time. That energy comes and goes—some days I’m wound up, others, I can’t get out of bed. But the voices, the figures, the chrome net—that’s been steady. I can’t tell if I’m sick in mind or just… seen too much.
D005-D006_h019.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D005-D006_h019.answer: B & D. Schizophrenia & Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D005-D006_h020.question:
I’ve been feeling off for about three months now. Ever since I came back from my last voyage, things just haven’t felt right. I keep hearing voices—sometimes whispering, sometimes calling my name—when no one’s around. At first, I thought it was the radio interference playing tricks on me, but it happens even at home. I’ve started noticing little things—neighbors closing their doors when I walk by, a plane flying overhead in a strange pattern—and I can’t shake the feeling they’re sending me messages, meant only for me.  

My wife says I’ve become quiet, distant. She’s right. I don’t feel like doing much—haven’t fixed the boat like I used to, haven’t even touched my logbook. But then, there are nights I barely sleep, full of energy, pacing, flipping through charts for hours. I don’t feel tired, like I could set sail right then. But those times don’t last. The voices come back. The thoughts jump—sailing, then the stars, then my father’s old watch, then back to the voices.  

I can’t tell you how long the high spells really last—some days, maybe a week total? Hard to say. And the voices… they’ve been there longer. But is it one illness or two mixed together? I don’t know. I just know I’m not myself.
D005-D006_h020.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D005-D006_h020.answer: B & D. Schizophrenia & Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D005-D006_h021.question:
I’ve been off since about three months ago, maybe a bit longer. At first, I thought it was just stress—my job’s monotonous, sitting in that booth all day, taking cash, smiling at drivers who barely look up. But then I started smelling things… like rotten eggs or burning hair. Nothing was there. I’d wipe down the booth, clean the vents—nothing. Now I can’t trust my own nose.

And my heart—I’m convinced something’s wrong with it. Not like a heart attack, but deeper. Like it’s shrinking. The doctor said the EKG was fine, but I know. I feel it thumping differently. Sometimes I adjust how I sit, or move my arms a certain way—it’s like I have to compensate. My coworkers noticed me twisting in the seat, doing little rituals, but they don’t get it. It’s not attention-seeking. It’s just… necessary.

I had a week last month where I barely slept, but I wasn’t tired. In fact, I felt sharp—wired. I cleaned the whole house at 3 a.m., called old friends, even thought about applying for a management job, which isn’t like me. But it passed. Now I’m back to feeling foggy, like I’m watching myself from behind glass. That part hasn’t stopped.
D005-D006_h021.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
D005-D006_h021.answer: A & C. Schizophrenia & Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D005-D006_h022.question:
I’ve been working nights at the corner store for about a year now, and things started feeling… off, around three months ago. At first, I thought it was just the isolation, the quiet hours, but then I began noticing things. I’d get this crawling feeling on my skin, like bugs moving under my shirt, but when I’d check, there’s nothing. I showered more, changed clothes, but it doesn’t stop. Sometimes, I feel something grabbing my arm, but no one’s there.

I’ve also been convinced lately that everything’s going to collapse—society, the world. Not like a fear, but a *knowing*. Like, it’s already over, and we’re just stuck in the echo. I don’t see the point in planning, in doing much of anything. My manager asked me to stock a shelf twice and I just stood there. Not because I didn’t hear him, but because… what’s the point if it’ll all vanish?

There are times I feel wired, like I don’t need sleep, like I could run for hours. I talk fast, think fast—but it doesn’t last. Maybe a few days, then it fades. I can’t say how long exactly. But even when that energy’s gone, the buzzing under my skin? That stays.
D005-D006_h022.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
D005-D006_h022.answer: A & C. Schizophrenia & Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D005-D006_h023.question:
I’ve been feeling off for about three months now—maybe longer, it’s hard to track. Things don’t feel real sometimes. There’s this taste in my mouth all the time, like metal or something spoiled, even when I haven’t eaten. Doctors can’t find anything wrong, but I *know* something’s happening inside me. I think something’s wrong with my stomach—like it’s rotting or not processing food the way it should. I checked myself in the mirror, poked at it… nothing looks different, but it *feels* wrong.

Sometimes when I’m sitting still, especially during stakeouts, I get this weird sensation like my body isn’t mine. Last week, a nurse tried to adjust my arm during an exam, and it just… stayed where she moved it, like warm wax. Felt strange, but I didn’t fight it.

I’ve had bursts of energy—times when I couldn’t sleep, wanted to take on five cases at once, talk fast, feel like I’m thinking ten steps ahead. But those don’t last long. Maybe a few days here and there. Then it fades, but the thoughts—the taste, the stomach, the numbness—those stick around. I don’t know what’s real anymore. My ex said I was “losing it,” but I’m not sure she understands.
D005-D006_h023.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D006_h024.question:
I’ve been struggling for about three months now—things just feel… off. I keep hearing whispers when no one’s around, like people are talking about me just behind the wall, but when I turn, there’s nothing. Sometimes they say the world’s already ended, that everything’s been wiped out and we’re just ghosts going through the motions. I know that sounds crazy, but it feels so real. I can’t ignore it.

I also catch myself making faces—my mouth twists sometimes, and I don’t even realize it until a coworker gives me a strange look. I work in a lab, analyzing evidence, but I’ve had to take days off because I can’t focus. The thoughts are loud. There was a week a while back where I barely slept, but I wasn’t tired—just wired, like I could process a month’s worth of data in one night. I felt sharp, too sharp. But that didn’t last long. Now I just feel numb, like I’m stuck between two states and can’t get out. I don’t know if I’m losing my mind or if the world actually changed and I’m the only one who sees it.

A. Schizophrenia
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D006_h025.question:
I’ve been struggling for about three months now—ever since I got back from a long-haul route. At first, I thought it was just exhaustion. But then I started feeling things—like worms crawling under my skin, especially on my arms and back. I’d scratch until I bled, but there was never anything there. I stopped wearing long sleeves because I thought my body was rotting inside, like my organs were turning to dust. Doctors ran tests, but they all came back fine. They don’t understand.

There are times when I just… can’t talk. Not because I don’t want to, but my throat closes up, like words are stuck. My crew noticed. They’d ask if I was okay, and I’d just stare. One time, I laughed for no reason during a safety briefing—just burst out laughing—but I don’t remember why. It felt like my mind was racing, like I could do ten things at once, but then the next day, I’d lie in bed for hours, mute, frozen.

The energy comes and goes. I’ll clean my apartment at 3 a.m., rearrange everything, feel unstoppable—then crash. But the crawling, the silence, the fear about my body—they’ve stayed. I don’t know what’s real anymore.
D005-D006_h025.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
D005-D006_h025.answer: A & C. Schizophrenia & Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
